title: Unproven precondition: luafv moves the parent the same way on Windows 10, and in %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

C2 (derived from the title): the same is measured in %ProgramFiles% (and %ProgramFiles(x86)%): missing
C3 (derived from the title): it is measured whether the parent moves the same way on Windows 10 (C:\Windows\Temp, and the C1/C2 locations): missing

rescan-same-windows-temp-tree-moves-again: Re-back-dated re-scans at +180 s and +20 min moved root, plain, links again; +30 s un-back-dated: none

Where the Fact lives: inside LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests, whose name says SystemRoot, so it reuses the class's helpers and the existing filter. The alternative is its own class (e.g. LastAccessOutsideTheWindowsFolderTests), which reads more honestly but needs the filter widened and the helpers shared.

Root shape: a fixed <CommonApplicationData>\fsa-tests parent left in place (this design, consistent with the class's other roots). Spike #2's measured alternative is a unique per-run fsa-tests-<guid> parent, removed with a non-recursive Directory.Delete, which leaves nothing permanent in a machine-wide folder.

Whether the SL-097 doc records the investigation's C:\Windows-outside-Temp data (7 of 12 parents moved; Tasks and tracing did not) as evidence beside the open Q-208, or leaves it to whichever slice takes Q-208.
Whether the numbers belong in a new SL-097 doc or are folded into the SL-096 doc's limits section.

Windows 10 measurement (C3): no Windows 10 machine here, and the Sandbox is Windows 11 26100 with EnableLUA=0 where luafv refuses to load (error 1275). Filed for a person; the command is in the SL-097 doc.
Elevated scan with luafv loaded in %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%: needs an administrator. Filed for a person.

A %ProgramFiles% or %ProgramFiles(x86)% fixture or standing probe: a standard user cannot create a tree there, and probing existing folders would move real install folders' last access on every run. The verdict is recorded from the existing-folder measurements.
A re-scan test and a re-scan limit sentence in ScanResult.cs: the existing 'counted out even when nothing moved' gap already covers it, and LastAccessKept is internal (Q-159).

A fitness rule or plant row for the %ProgramData% root or for 'nothing corrects outside %SystemRoot%': the design declares none, and widening Scanner.cs:340 is caught behaviourally by the new Fact (mutation run: red at 'kept 4 of 7').

A person with a Windows 10 PC runs the command in docs/design/SL-097-last-access-outside-the-windows-folder.md (the LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests, LastAccessTests and HeldOpenTreeTests filter) and reports every 'moved:' line (Q-205).
A person with an administrator token measures an elevated scan with luafv loaded in %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%, only if LastAccessKept stops being internal (Q-159) or the app is run elevated.
Q-208: the SL-097 doc records the investigation's C:\Windows-outside-Temp data (7 of 12 parents moved; Tasks and tracing did not) for whichever slice takes it.
The CloudRig and SyncRootRig still root in the inherited temp folder and are exempt by name from the route rule (SL-096). That exemption is out of scope here.
C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests stays as an empty folder visible to every user. Remove it by hand if that is unwanted, or switch to a per-run parent as spike #2 measured.

deviation: Review m2 and the design said 'TempTree(string) used unchanged'. The named create-refusal is built in TempTree.CreateRoot, around Directory.CreateDirectory only, not around the whole call from the constructor. TempTree(string) and the default TempTree() both reach it, so both deliberate roots get it. A failure of the compression branch's Directory.Delete is then not mislabelled as 'could not create'. The compression InvalidOperationException passes through unwrapped.

deviation: ChooseProgramDataTestsRoot also refuses when the Windows folder is blank or not fully qualified, not only when CommonApplicationData is bad. The design's refusal needs a Windows folder to compare against, and failing closed is red with a cause, never a vacuous pass.

deviation: Added TheMeasuredLastAccessLimitIsWrittenWhereTheTreeSaidUnmeasured, a small prose pin, because O-006/C-006 needs a test the engine can run and the design's check was a Select-String command. It also holds review M1's requirement that the SL-097 doc says no 'falsified'.

deviation: Added tests in TempTreeRootTests and TempTreeTests so C-009 (a bad known folder) and review m2 (a refused create) are fed by real tests. Neither needs an ACL change: the create refusal uses a tests root whose parent is a file.

deviation: Resolved the design's taste disagreements as the design leaned: the Fact lives in LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests, the root is a fixed <CommonApplicationData>\fsa-tests parent left in place, the numbers are in a new SL-097 doc rather than folded into the SL-096 doc, and the C:\Windows-outside-Temp data (7 of 12 moved; Tasks and tracing did not) is recorded as evidence for Q-208 and not acted on.
deviation: No KnownWorkarounds entry or setting was added: this slice adds no step-around of an outside defect. It decides not to extend an internal counter correction (Q-159).

drift: Nothing undeclared departed. The six declared deviations all match the tree: - CreateRoot wrap at the seam; - refusal of a Windows folder that cannot be told; - the prose pin test; - the C-009 and m2 tests; - the taste choices; - no KnownWorkarounds entry.

drift: For the next reader, the design's recalled claim is now measured. GetFolderPath(CommonApplicationData) survives a host that strips ProgramData, ALLUSERSPROFILE or SystemDrive one at a time. With six location variables stripped together it returns blank, and the Fact then fails closed with 'it is blank'.
not reached: Windows 10, in every location: no Windows 10 machine here. The Sandbox (Windows 11 26100, EnableLUA=0) blocks luafv (error 1275). Person-run: the command is in the SL-097 doc.

not reached: An elevated scan with luafv loaded in %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%: it needs a session running the project's code as an administrator, which neither named operation provides. Not needed while the app never runs elevated and LastAccessKept is internal (Q-159).

not reached: My own fresh re-measure of %ProgramFiles% and %ProgramFiles(x86)%: every candidate parent's last access was 0.60 h old, under NTFS's 1-hour rule, so nothing was opened. Their verdict rests on the survey's and investigation's measurements from earlier today.

not reached: A same-mask positive control on existing C:\Windows folders: the scanner's 0x101 was refused there (error 5), so my control used 0x2 while the %ProgramData% probes used 0x101. The same-mask 0x101 move under C:\Windows\Temp comes from the project's own Fact runs.
not reached: Stability of the %ProgramData% Fact against Defender or the indexer over days or weeks: only about 9 clean runs today on one machine.
not reached: A machine where C:\ProgramData itself refuses folder creation by this user: only simulated with a deny rule on a folder in my own temp.

critique missed: The design's case for a tests root refused by its ACL was marked not material on the premise that feeding it 'means changing C:\ProgramData's ACL'. Critique 1 and 2 accepted that premise, and critique 2 asked only for the create-refusal wrap in the seam. They did not ask for a test that raises UnauthorizedAccessException, which Q-210 named and which the existing TempTree.Deny(path, 0x4) (TempTree.cs:281) can raise inside a test's own temp tree with no system ACL change. The build's refusal test fed only an IOException (a parent that is a file), so a mutant narrowing CreateRoot's catch to IOException survives the suite.

code-review missed: Round 1 confirmed the prose pin TheMeasuredLastAccessLimitIsWrittenWhereTheTreeSaidUnmeasured. It checked that the pinned phrases were new in the diff and sat on one line, but not what spellings of the retracted claim it still allowed. The pin bans only 'falsified' and requires 'Windows 10'. M1's wrong wording was 'shows no under-count', so a record that restates that, says 'disproved', or drops the +30 s re-scan section stays green. The builder's 'A test pins all of it' rested on a mutant that inserted exactly the banned word.

still unknown: Does Windows 10 move a child folder's parent in C:\Windows\Temp, %ProgramData% or %ProgramFiles%? If it does not move them in Windows\Temp, the five SL-096 Facts go red by Q-210's ruling because the structural correction would under-count. If it moves them in %ProgramData%, InProgramDataNoKeptFolderMovesItsParent goes red and the scanner over-counts. Only a person with a Windows 10 PC can run the SL-097 doc's command (Q-205).

still unknown: Does an elevated scan with luafv loaded move parents in %ProgramData% or %ProgramFiles%? This matters only if LastAccessKept stops being internal (Q-159) or the app is run elevated. The Sandbox cannot answer it (luafv blocked, error 1275).

still unknown: Q-208: under C:\Windows outside Temp, 7 of 12 pre-existing parents moved, but Tasks and tracing did not. The correction fires for all of %SystemRoot%, so LastAccessKept can still under-count there. The data is recorded in the SL-097 doc for whoever takes Q-208.

still unknown: Is InProgramDataNoKeptFolderMovesItsParent stable against Defender or the indexer over days and weeks? Only about 9 clean runs on one machine today (3 in a row, 2 TEMP values, the full suite, validate). A touch on the tree between back-dating and the scan would show as a red in the default suite.

still unknown: Is the %ProgramFiles% non-elevated verdict real beyond one folder? One of 10,442 folders (depth 3 AccessCheck walk) was write-grantable, EaseUS Data Recovery Wizard\ensdata, and its parent did not move. Validate's fresh re-measure was skipped on the unproven one-hour rule.

went wrong: Risk-spike halted with 2 held and 1 no-go, and needed a person pass. The no-go was on the investigation's re-scan hypothesis, which the design never intended to build. The spike's yardstick (kept vs still-old) could not detect an under-count on a re-scan, so its own 'no under-count' reading was wrong.

went wrong: The person's proceed-note ('limit is false and is not to be written') over-stated spike #3. The design copied 'falsified' into its rationale, outside_claims and doc plan. Critique M1 (major) had to re-read the raw evidence to correct it. The built SL-097 doc was fixed, but the guard test for it banned only that one word (R2-m2, waived to SC-186). One misreading cost the spike, the design, the critique and a second code-review round.

went wrong: The design stated two false things about the tree: that the existing guard 'now covers the new Fact' (LastAccessRuleCorpusTests.cs:90-95 pins three names) and that SL-096 had built a create-refusal wrap (TempTree.CreateRoot was bare). Both were critique majors/minors (M2, m2). The designer had not been handed the guard test or the TempTree seam.

went wrong: Critique ran twice: round 1 halted with 4 findings, all later accepted as real, then a model disposed of them. Code review also ran twice. Round 1 let the narrow prose pin through (R2-m2). The ACL refusal gap (SC-185) was found by code review and validate, not by the critique that had ruled the case not material.

went wrong: The build-check's 'confounded by the NTFS one-hour rule' verdict on the scratch probe was reasoning, not measurement, and spike #1 contradicted it. Validate then applied the same rule to skip the fresh %ProgramFiles% re-measure, so that verdict still rests on 0 of 1 earlier survey folder.

went wrong: The survey lost its like-for-like fresh %ProgramData% control twice because the engine refuses Remove-Item on system paths. It had to fall back to existing-folder probes, whose candidate sets overlap with the investigation's and cannot be summed.

went wrong: Q-206 (answered: the SL-096 doc 'exists nowhere') predated the SL-096 merge (989c119) and was wrong by the time this slice ran. The design caught it and the answer still stands uncorrected on the question list.
went wrong: Windows 10 and the elevated scan are still unmeasured after two slices. This slice delivered the Win11 non-elevated verdict and the hand-off command only.
